articles.title: Walking across my Minecraft backups with Plakar
articles.summary: Plakar is an open-source backup solution that allows developers to create backups of their Minecraft servers without stopping them, pausing world saves over Remote Console (RCON) while the backup runs and allowing players to keep digging. The solution is built on top of kloset, a content-addressed storage engine that deduplicates, compresses and encrypts everything it stores and keeps snapshots immutable. Plakar backs up from a variety of sources, stores on multiple storages, and restores to multiple destinations, including a filesystem, S3 bucket, and SFTP server. The project has written 45 connectors so far, with most targeting general consumer products and tools, and the author plans to use an AI to generate more connectors to show that there's no excuse not to protect data, even for non-programmers.

An EMP is a short, high-voltage pulse that can damage long conductors like transformers, but unplugged electronics are generally safe. The 2008 report on EMPs from the Commission to Assess the Threat to the United States from Electromagnetic Pulse Attack suggests that most common devices are fine as long as they're off and unplugged. Leaving equipment off and unplugged is likely enough to protect it from an EMP, but it's not a foolproof solution and developers should consider other precautions as well.
